newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates higher in tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates higher in tight liquidity.

text.p: * Bank funds tied up in dollars, T-bills
Philippine overnight money edged higher for the second straight day on Tuesday as the tight liquidity situation continued to persist, traders said.
The average rate rose to 12.15625 percent from 11.96875. Volume swelled to 28.792 billion pesos from 24.028 billion pesos.
"There are still a lot of borrowers," a dealer said.
Of 66 participating financial insitutions, 39 were lenders.

One dealer explained bank funds had been tied up in dollars because of expectations the peso would continue to weaken. Banks had also invested in Treasury bills ahead of a further slide in interest rates, she said.
Banks expect liquidity to ease only by next week when their termed reverse repos mature, the dealer added.
There was little trading activityin the secondary market for T-bills.
